title: Anglo-American legal history
audience: a pre-law college student (any major) preparing for law school and the LSAT
purpose: Trace the common law from medieval England to the modern United States: royal courts and juries, equity, Magna Carta, the English constitution, colonial law, the Constitution and Bill of Rights, slavery and Reconstruction, codification, the New Deal and the civil rights era.
primary_reading: Yale Avalon Project: documents in law, history and diplomacy

weeks.1: Roman and medieval roots of law
weeks.2: The Norman Conquest and the royal courts
weeks.4: Equity and the Court of Chancery
weeks.5: Magna Carta and the rule of law
weeks.6: The English Civil War and the Glorious Revolution
weeks.9: Slavery, the Civil War and the Reconstruction amendments
weeks.10: Industrialization, codification and the Progressive Era
weeks.11: The New Deal and the administrative state
weeks.12: The civil rights era and modern constitutional law

blocks.deliverable: Explain how the common law got its name.
Compare a remedy at law with a remedy in equity.
Trace one clause of Magna Carta to the Bill of Rights.
Week 7 midterm; explain the reasoning of Marbury v. Madison.
Explain the purposes of the 13th, 14th and 15th Amendments.
Build a timeline connecting five landmark cases to their era.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Document-based history paper: using primary sources supplied in the project, explain how one institution (for example trial by jury or habeas corpus) developed from England to the modern United States, in 1,800 words.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
